title: Adhesives
headline:
THE RIGHT BOND
STARTS WITH THE APPLICATION.
summary: Adhesive solutions for construction, manufacturing and industrial assembly.
heading: Bonding across different materials.
body: NAPCO’s published adhesive portfolio covers hot-melt, instant and pressure-sensitive adhesives, thread-lockers and structural adhesives for construction and industrial applications.

The current product overview identifies acrylic, epoxy and urethane technologies and describes bonding across substrates including bare and painted metal, composites and rubber-to-substrate assemblies.
Selection should begin with the substrates, joint design, production method and conditions in use. Product-specific suitability still needs to be confirmed against current technical documentation.

FOCUS ON
THE JOINT.
summary: Sealing solutions for construction and industrial applications.
heading: Built around the application.
body: NAPCO develops sealants for construction, automotive and transport, manufacturing, maintenance and repair. Its technical support approach starts with the customer’s requirements.

The published portfolio is developed through consultation with customers and people involved in application. Discuss the joint, materials and operating conditions with NAPCO before choosing a product.

title: Coatings
headline:
CONSIDER
THE SURFACE.
summary: Coating solutions for construction, manufacturing, restoration and rebuilding.
heading: Protection begins with the surface.
body: NAPCO’s coating portfolio covers construction and industrial applications. Its published examples include building panels, roofs, concrete floors and walls, HVAC, furniture and commercial appliances.
Research and development considers production requirements alongside the needs of the finished surface. Discuss the substrate, intended use and relevant product data with the technical team.

title: Construction solutions
headline:
BIG IDEAS.
SMALL DETAILS.
summary: Adhesives, sealants and coatings across building and renovation.
heading: Build. Protect. Finish. Repair.
body: NAPCO organises its construction offer around four stages: Build, Protect, Finish and Repair. The live construction overview describes products used under floors, behind walls and within building structures.
Published applications include waterproof bonding and sealing, foundation and basement damp-proofing, swimming-pool applications, roofing, bonding agents, grouts, sealants and coatings.
Use the four application stages to frame the project requirement, then confirm the actual system and product against current technical information.

START WITH
THE STRUCTURE.
summary: Material and application thinking for new construction.
heading: Plan the materials with the build.
body: NAPCO’s published Build page starts at the planning stage of a structure and describes collaboration with architects, engineers and project teams.
The live site references concrete and cement, grout, structural adhesives, bonding agents, waterproofing, roofing, sealants and coatings as part of the construction discussion.
Use the structural detail, substrates, construction sequence and required technical documentation to define the next step.

title: Protect
headline:
PROTECTION STARTS
WITH THE EXPOSURE.
summary: Protection, moisture and sealing considerations for construction.
heading: Understand what the structure is exposed to.
body: NAPCO’s current construction overview describes waterproof bonding and sealing, foundation and basement damp-proofing, swimming-pool applications, roofing and other measures intended to limit moisture migration.
The protection requirement changes with the substrate, location and exposure. A below-grade interface, roof detail and wet-area application should not be treated as the same problem.
Define the exposure and construction detail first, then confirm the appropriate system against current NAPCO technical information.

title: Finish

THE FINISH BEGINS
WITH THE SURFACE.
summary: Surface-led thinking for construction finishing applications.
heading: Connect the finish with the substrate.
body: NAPCO’s construction portfolio includes adhesives, sealants and coatings used to prepare, bond, seal and protect building materials through the finishing stages of a project.
The finished appearance is only one part of the requirement. Surface condition, material compatibility, installation sequence and expected exposure all influence the application discussion.
Start with the substrate and intended finish, then review the relevant current technical documentation.

REPAIR STARTS WITH
THE EXISTING CONDITION.

heading: Understand what has changed before repairing it.
body: NAPCO’s published Repair page frames renovation and repair as a way to extend the usable life of buildings and infrastructure.

The live page describes repair requirements from below-ground areas to rooftops, inside and outside the structure. The existing condition, substrate and cause of failure therefore need to be understood before material selection.
Use current technical information to match the repair scope with the appropriate product or system.

BUILT FOR
COMPLEX ASSEMBLIES.
summary: Adhesives, sealants and coatings for automotive and transport applications.
heading: Look inside the assembly.
body: NAPCO’s automotive and transport material portfolio spans multiple manufacturing steps rather than a single bond line. Its published overview references interiors, exteriors, electronics, body assembly, trim and aftersales applications.

The live site also describes applications across the press shop, paint division and assembly process, including metalworking fluids, adhesives, sealants, metal coatings, pre-treatment and repair solutions.
The relevant formulation depends on the component, substrates, production process and end-use conditions. Those application details should lead the technical discussion.

Its published applications include wood-to-wood assembly, edge banding, edge-to-edge gluing, finger jointing and bonding wood to metal or other dissimilar materials.
Start with the actual wood-based material, adjacent substrate, production process and service environment, then confirm the relevant adhesive and current product documentation.

CRAFT MEETS
CHEMISTRY.

Wood, MDF and other materials each bring different requirements. Start with the component and manufacturing process, then review the appropriate adhesive and its current documentation.

SOLUTIONS FOR

Published examples extend into metalworking, cable-related applications, fluid-leak prevention, noise and vibration control and sealing requirements exposed to temperature, pressure or movement.
The material decision should be tied to the production step, substrates and finished assembly. Current technical data remains the basis for product-specific selection.

Its published technology references include water-based adhesives, toluene-free adhesives, cyanoacrylates, hot-melt and PUR hot-melt systems for varied production requirements.

Published examples include metal, glass, foams and low-surface-energy plastics, together with mounting, trim, badges, gaskets and seals, control panels, coils, glass doors and cooktops.

title: About NAPCO
headline:
CONSISTENT QUALITY.
APPLICATION-LED THINKING.
summary: Company context, history, people and regional application knowledge.
heading: A company built around materials and relationships.
body: NAPCO’s current corporate site presents the company around adhesives, coatings and sealants for construction and industrial markets, supported by technical expertise and research and development.
Its published corporate themes include history, vision and goals, NAPCO World, regional presence, corporate culture, leadership, milestones and brands.
The new website brings those themes into a clearer application-led structure while preserving the established promise of consistent quality delivered through innovation.

title: History
headline:
BUILT OVER TIME.
STILL MOVING FORWARD.
summary: Key steps in NAPCO’s manufacturing and materials journey.
heading: From technical services to manufacturing.
body: NAPCO’s published History page says NAPCO Industries (UK) has been involved in adhesives manufacturing since 1988 and that a UAE manufacturing facility was established in 1995.
The same page records the introduction of solvent-borne adhesives in 1998, sealants in 2003 and an independent production facility in 2007.
The important website story is the evolution of capabilities over time: adhesives, coatings and sealants developed alongside changing construction and industrial requirements.

topics.description: The published history records the establishment of a UAE manufacturing facility.
Solvent-borne adhesives and then sealant production were added.

headline:
APPLICATIONS THAT
TOUCH EVERYDAY LIFE.
summary: A broad materials portfolio supporting construction and industrial applications.
heading: From everyday objects to complex production.
body: NAPCO’s published company material describes adhesives, sealants and coatings used across everyday products and industrial processes, from books and packaging to vehicles, appliances, furniture and electronics.
The company positions application knowledge and research-and-development capability as part of how it works with customers across manufacturing and construction.
The practical website route is therefore application-led: identify the materials, process and performance requirement first, then move into the relevant product family and technical information.

The published approach emphasises understanding local customer needs, assessing partners and using regional market knowledge to support product and application decisions.
For the new website, regional presence should be presented as a route to local application conversations rather than as an unverified claim of universal coverage.

PEOPLE WHO BUILD
THE NEXT SOLUTION.

The company says employees are encouraged to develop and propose ideas, while training and development support future technical and leadership capability.
The corporate site also describes long-term, mutually beneficial relationships as a central part of NAPCO’s culture.

title: Milestones & achievements
headline:
A JOURNEY OF
CAPABILITY BUILDING.
summary: Published milestones in NAPCO’s manufacturing development.
heading: A timeline of expanding capability.
body: NAPCO’s current corporate material records the UAE manufacturing facility in 1995, the addition of solvent-borne adhesives in 1998, sealant production in 2003 and an independent production facility in 2007.
These milestones are useful because they show how the company broadened its technical and manufacturing scope over time.
Earlier-year references differ between the live History and Milestones pages, so the new site intentionally avoids reproducing the conflicting pre-1995 date until it is verified.

topics.description: UAE manufacturing is recorded as a major step in the published history.

title: Innovation strategy
headline:
TECHNICAL THINKING.
PRACTICAL RELEVANCE.
summary: A materials-focused approach to customer application challenges.
heading: Innovation starts with a real requirement.
body: NAPCO describes its innovation strategy as centred on material science and customer application challenges. Its research and development work addresses functional materials, polymer building blocks and adhesive-bonding processes.
The published strategy also identifies reverse engineering as part of its development approach, alongside formulation and manufacturing work for adhesives, coatings and sealants.
The strongest role for the website is to connect that technical thinking to a real requirement: the materials, process, constraints and end use that define the application.

IMPROVEMENT ACROSS
THE VALUE CHAIN.

heading: Supply chain, operations and future direction.
body: NAPCO’s current sustainability material is organised around supply chain, sustainable operations and future targets.

The supply-chain section describes expectations around integrity, quality, collaboration and continuous improvement. The operations section discusses low-VOC development, resource efficiency and customer/supplier involvement as themes.

The published Targets page sets a 2030 ambition for key suppliers to demonstrate positive sustainability contribution. This and any environmental performance claims should be revalidated before production publication.

If the application or product requirement is not yet clear, the live site directs customers to contact NAPCO for help, to locate a distributor, request a quote or discuss a sample.
